correctness.rationale: Forth means that both Boolean truth sets are upsets; onto forces bottom and top to their respective images. At a maximal common zero, a first cover on a saturated chain to a lift of either singleton must already have that singleton image. Conversely, every common zero lies below a maximal one, and the two covers at that maximal zero give both singleton lifts. Top and reflexivity handle all other required lifts, and the endpoint and cover witnesses ensure surjectivity. This proves the all-n finite sum. A coordinate projection gives existence for n>=2, and the cardinality obstruction at n=1 is decisive. The independent enumeration generates upsets by antichains and tests down-closures of the singleton fibres at every zero, not the maximal-cover condition. It partitions the accepted pairs under the source atom permutations after quotienting by target swap, rather than using Burnside fixed sums. Labelled counts 0, 2, 30, 1086, 288524 and orbit counts 0, 1, 5, 50, 1918 all reproduced. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproduce_4.py, output /workspace/reproduce_4.txt. The frozen C and Python programs and outputs were inspected; the fresh replay did not execute them.

value.rationale: The diamond is the smallest Boolean lattice with incomparable worlds, so both atomic lifts at a common zero give the first Boolean-target case not modeled by a chain. The exact labelled and orbit enumerations, through 7581 monotone functions at n=5, give reproducible finite quotients for this natural family and distinguish symmetry types from counts of indexed maps. Value is in this complete initial census linked to the lifting obstruction, not in the routine coordinate representation or a claimed formula beyond n=5.
